mainTopic: ראשית הגז: proving that a מנה of forty סלעים exists, how the five-סלע measure is weighed, and the פסוק source for the 'small garment' measure (the אבנט).
overview: The amud opens by finishing a line from the previous page about a weight of sixty סלעים. It then proves that a תנא really speaks of a מנה worth forty סלעים, using רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's words about a torn leather flask. Next the גמרא explains the משנה's measure for ראשית הגז. The five סלעים are weighed after washing, but the כהן does the washing, not the owner. The 'small garment' measure comes from 'לעמד לשרת': the gift must be enough for an אבנט. The אבנט is chosen over the bigger מעיל because we take the smaller amount. The wool כיפה does not count because 'הוא ובניו' requires a garment shared by all כהנים, and every כהן wears something called a 'belt.' Then רב חסדא and רבי נתן בר הושעיא disagree about someone who shears each sheep and then sells it. Last, the גמרא asks which תנא says the obligation follows a seller who kept some wool. רב חסדא's answer, רבי יהודה's ruling on פאה, is rejected by רבא. רבא brings instead the משנה about buying a cow's innards that contain the priestly gifts.

steps.title: End of the previous line: a weight of sixty
steps.stepSummary: The text opens with the last word of a statement that started on the previous page. That statement speaks of a weight of sixty סלעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...in sixty [סלעים].
steps.whatsHappening: This is just the closing word of a sentence that began before this page. It tells us the earlier statement spoke about a weight of sixty סלעים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier calculation uses a unit called a מנה. This one word wraps that statement up. It sets up the next question, which asks about a different-sized מנה.

keyTerms.meaning: A coin and a unit of weight. Many measures in this סוגיא are counted in סלעים.

phrases.english: in sixty [sela],
phrases.notes: This word finishes a sentence from the previous page. Read it as 'weighing sixty סלעים.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a statement that began on the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The earlier statement refers to a weight of sixty סלעים.

steps.title: Does any teacher speak of a forty-sela maneh?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether any תנא actually teaches that a מנה can be worth forty סלעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But does a תנא really teach about a מנה of forty סלעים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to check one detail. Do we ever find a תנא who speaks of a מנה equal to forty סלעים?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The calculation being discussed relies on a מנה of forty סלעים. The גמרא wants to make sure this measure really shows up in an early source and was not simply made up.

keyTerms.meaning: A larger unit of weight or money, made up of a set number of סלעים.
A teacher from the time of the משנה.

phrases.english: But does a tanna teach:
a maneh of forty sela?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whether the forty-סלע מנה used in the calculation has an early source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is there an early source that speaks of a מנה of forty סלעים?

steps.title: Yes: the torn leather flask teaching
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers yes. It brings a teaching about a leather flask in which רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says outright, 'a מנה of forty סלעים.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes! We learned: a new leather flask, even if it can hold pomegranates, is טהור. If it was sewn and then tore, the size of the tear is big enough for pomegranates to fall out. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: the size of balls of warp thread, each one a quarter of a מנה of forty סלעים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says 'Yes!' and proves it. The proof is a teaching about the size of a tear in a leather flask, where a תנא uses a 'מנה of forty סלעים' as his measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The main subject of the teaching is טומאה of a leather flask, but the proof comes from one detail. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב measures the tear by thread-balls, each weighing a quarter of a 'מנה of forty סלעים.' That phrase shows a תנא really used this measure.

keyTerms.meaning: A leather flask or bag for holding liquids.
Not able to become טמא (ritually impure).
The set measure or size the law requires.
Balls of warp thread (the threads that run the long way on a loom).

steps.confusionAlert: Don't get pulled into the topic of the flask itself. The גמרא only brings this teaching for the words 'a מנה of forty סלעים' at the very end.

phrases.english: Yes! And we learned:
A new leather flask,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמְּקַבֶּלֶת רִמּוֹנִים – טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.english: even though it can hold pomegranates, is not susceptible to impurity.
phrases.notes: It is not finished yet, since it cannot hold liquid. So it does not yet count as a כלי.

phrases.english: If he sewed it and it tore,
its measure is a hole that lets pomegranates fall out.
Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov says:
like the size of balls of warp thread,
each one a quarter,
of a maneh of forty sela.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by citing a source that mentions the forty-סלע מנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב speaks of 'a מנה of forty סלעים' in the teaching about a torn flask.
steps.raayaObject: That a forty-סלע מנה is a real measure used by a תנא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching about a torn leather flask (from the תוספתא), in the words of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.whatToRemember: A מנה of forty סלעים is a real measure. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב uses it when he measures the tear in a leather flask.

steps.title: Five sela measured after washing, but the priest does the washing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about how much wool goes to the כהן. A ברייתא explains that the owner does not have to wash it himself. He gives enough that after the כהן washes it, it still weighs five סלעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'And how much does he give him...' A ברייתא teaches: it does not mean he must wash the wool and then give it. It means the כהן will wash it, and it must still come to five סלעים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה, about how much wool the כהן gets. A ברייתא clears up what 'laundered' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says five סלעים 'laundered,' which could sound like the owner must wash it first. The ברייתא says no: the owner gives the wool unwashed. He just has to give enough that after the כהן washes it, it still weighs five סלעים. The point is the weight after washing, not who does the washing.

keyTerms.meaning: That he washes (whitens) it.
A priest, who receives ראשית הגז (the first shearing of the wool).
And it will come out to / still amount to.

phrases.english: "And how much does he give him" etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' points to the rest of the משנה line: five סלעים in יהודה, ten in the גליל, laundered and not dirty.

phrases.english: A baraita taught: not that he launders it and gives it to him,
but rather that the priest launders it
and it amounts to five sela.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה and starts a new topic: how the wool given to the כהן is measured.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The five סלעים are counted after washing, but the כהן does the washing, not the owner.

steps.title: Where does the 'small garment' measure come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's phrase 'enough to make a small garment' and asks what the source for it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'enough to make a small garment.' From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another phrase from the משנה and asks for its source. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה ties the size of the gift to making a garment. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches that the amount depends on making a garment at all.

keyTerms.meaning: A small garment.
From where are these things learned? (a request for a source)

phrases.english: "Enough to make a small garment."
From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next phrase of the משנה and asks for its source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק teaches that the gift must be enough to make a garment?

steps.title: From 'to stand to serve': fit for the Temple service
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי learns it from the words 'לעמד לשרת.' The gift must be something fit to be used in the עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: The פסוק says, 'to stand to serve.' It must be something fit for service.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי gives the source. A פסוק near the מצוה of ראשית הגז speaks of the כהן standing 'to serve,' so the gift must be enough for something used in the עבודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'לשרת' (to serve) links the wool gift to the כהן's service in the בית המקדש. So the amount is not random. It has to be enough for something a כהן could actually use in his service.

keyTerms.meaning: A פסוק (verse).
To stand to serve: the words that describe the כהן's job.
Fit to be used in the Temple service.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
The verse states: "to stand to serve,"
phrases.notes: דברים 18:5

phrases.english: something that is fit for service.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'לעמד לשרת' teaches that the gift must be enough for something fit for the עבודה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the minimum size of the ראשית הגז gift. It must be enough to make something useful for the כהן's service.

steps.title: Which garment? The belt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which service garment is meant and answers right away: the אבנט, the כהן's belt.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it? The belt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which garment fits 'something fit for service' and answers at once: the אבנט (belt).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Of all the כהן's garments, the אבנט is the 'small garment' the משנה means. That ties the משנה's phrase 'small garment' to a specific item the כהן wears during the עבודה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it?
The belt, one of the כהן's garments.

steps.whatToRemember: The minimum gift of ראשית הגז is enough to make an אבנט, a garment worn in the עבודה. This comes from 'לעמד לשרת.'

phrases.english: What is it? The belt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Names the specific service garment the derivation refers to.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which garment fit for the עבודה is meant?

steps.title: Why not say the garment is the robe?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the choice of the אבנט and suggests the garment could be the מעיל instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say it is the robe!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer that the garment is the אבנט. It asks: maybe the פסוק means the מעיל, the robe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source 'לעמד לשרת' only tells us the gift must be fit for a garment used in the עבודה. The מעיל is also a service garment, so why pick the אבנט? Choosing the מעיל would require much more wool.

keyTerms.meaning: Say / maybe we should say (offers another possibility)
The robe of the כהן גדול, a large garment

phrases.english: Say it is the robe!
phrases.notes: The robe takes a lot more wool than a belt, so this would raise the amount the owner has to give.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the identification of the garment as the אבנט
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 7 that the service garment is the אבנט
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The מעיל is also a service garment, so nothing in 'לעמד לשרת' points to the אבנט specifically.

steps.title: Go with the smaller amount
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with the rule: if you grab too much you get nothing, if you grab a little you get it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you grasped a lot, you did not grasp. If you grasped a little, you grasped.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a well-known rule. When we are unsure how much is required, we go with the smaller amount that still fits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אבנט already meets the condition of being a service garment. Requiring the larger amount for a מעיל has no firm basis, but the smaller amount is certainly included. So the minimum is set by the אבנט.

keyTerms.meaning: If you grab a lot, you have not grabbed: going with the bigger option is not secure
A small amount

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is used all over the גמרא whenever a source could mean a larger or smaller amount.

phrases.english: If you grasped a lot, you did not grasp;
phrases.notes: Reach for too much and you might end up with nothing solid. The smaller choice is the safe one.

phrases.english: if you grasped a little, you grasped.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: General principle of interpretation (choose the minimum)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe the larger מעיל is meant.
steps.terutzMaskana: We take the smaller garment that qualifies, the אבנט.

steps.title: Why not the even smaller wool cap?
steps.stepSummary: Using the same logic, the גמרא suggests the כהן גדול's wool כיפה, which is smaller than the אבנט, and brings a ברייתא showing it existed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say it is the cap of wool. As a ברייתא teaches: a cap of wool was placed on the head of the כהן גדול, and the ציץ was placed on it, to fulfill the פסוק 'And you shall put it on a thread of sky blue.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the last answer around. If we want the smallest garment, the wool כיפה of the כהן גדול is even smaller than the אבנט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא proves this כיפה really was worn in the עבודה. It sat under the ציץ to fulfill 'פתיל תכלת.' Following 'grab the little amount,' the minimum should drop to the size of this cap.

keyTerms.meaning: A cap
The gold plate worn on the forehead of the כהן גדול
A thread of sky-blue wool
The High Priest

phrases.english: But say it is the cap of wool,
as it is taught: a cap of wool
was placed on the head of the High Priest,
and the frontplate was placed on it,
to fulfill what is said:
"And you shall put it on a thread of sky blue."
phrases.notes: שמות 28:37. The ברייתא reads the 'thread of sky blue' as this wool cap.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the principle from step 9 to argue for an even smaller garment
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice of the אבנט as the minimum
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If we always take the smaller amount, the wool כיפה is smaller than the אבנט and is also a service garment, as the ברייתא shows.

steps.title: It must be a garment shared by all כהנים
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'הוא ובניו,' so the garment must be one that אהרן and his sons both wear. The כיפה is worn only by the כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'he and his sons': something that is the same for אהרן and for his sons.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the same פסוק says 'הוא ובניו.' So the garment has to be one that both the כהן גדול and regular כהנים wear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the כהן גדול wears the wool כיפה, so it does not qualify. The אבנט, which every כהן wears, does. This rules out the cap and keeps the אבנט as the measure.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק
He and his sons: אהרן and the regular כהנים
Equal / the same for both

phrases.english: The verse says "he and his sons,"
phrases.notes: דברים 18:5. It is the same פסוק as 'לעמד לשרת' from the earlier step.

phrases.english: something that is equal for אהרן and for his sons.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Additional detail from the פסוק narrows the category
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The smallest service garment, the כיפה, should set the amount.
steps.terutzMaskana: The garment must be shared by all כהנים, so the כהן גדול's cap is excluded.

steps.title: The belt is not the same for all כהנים either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the אבנט also is not equal for the כהן גדול and a regular כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The belt is also not equal!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks its own answer. By the rule of 'הוא ובניו,' even the אבנט should not count, since it is not the same for all כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule from step 11 removed the כיפה because it was not shared. But the אבנט of the כהן גדול differs from the אבנט of a regular כהן. So the same rule seems to remove the אבנט too.

keyTerms.meaning: Also
Is not equal / not the same

phrases.english: The belt is also not equal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the rule of step 11 against the אבנט itself
steps.kashyaTarget: Identifying the garment as the אבנט (step 7)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the garment must be the same for all כהנים, the אבנט fails too, because the כהן גדול's belt differs from a regular כהן's.

steps.title: No problem according to one opinion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the objection is not a problem for the view that the כהן גדול's special belt is different from a regular כהן's belt. The real difficulty is for the other view.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works out well according to the one who says the belt of the כהן גדול is not the belt of a regular כהן. It is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It shows that one opinion has no problem, which prepares the question of what to say according to the other opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this view, the special belt the כהן גדול wears on יום כיפור is different. The regular כהן's belt matches the belt the כהן גדול wears the rest of the year, so the אבנט is shared after all. The difficulty from step 12 remains only for the opposite opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well (according to one view), hinting at a problem for the other view
A regular כהן
Well / fine

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'הניחא' as the final answer. It only clears one opinion; the problem still stands for the other side, and the גמרא will deal with that next.

phrases.english: This works out well according to the one who said
the belt of the High Priest

phrases.aramaic: לֹא זֶהוּ אַבְנֵטוֹ שֶׁל כֹּהֵן הֶדְיוֹט –
phrases.english: is not the belt of an ordinary priest –
phrases.notes: He means the special belt the כהן גדול wears on יום כיפור. His everyday belt is the same as a regular כהן's.

phrases.english: it is fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the objection of step 12 to only one opinion, setting up the continuation
steps.kashyaTarget: The אבנט as a garment shared by all כהנים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The objection works only against the view that the כהן גדול's belt and a regular כהן's belt are the same. For the opposing view, there is no difficulty.

steps.title: Every כהן has something called a belt
steps.stepSummary: Even for the view that the כהן גדול's year-round belt differs from a regular כהן's belt, the word 'belt' still applies to both, so the אבנט counts as a garment of 'אהרן and his sons.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the one who says the כהן גדול's יום כיפור belt is the same as a regular כהן's belt, what can we say? The name 'belt' exists for everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the hard question left over from the last step and answers it right away: every כהן wears some kind of belt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By this view, during the rest of the year the כהן גדול's wool-and-linen belt is different from a regular כהן's belt. The answer is that the פסוק only needs a garment called by the same name for אהרן and his sons, and 'belt' is shared by all of them. The כיפה has no such shared name, so it still does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: The belt worn by the כהנים
A regular כהן, not the כהן גדול
The name 'belt' applies to all of them

steps.whatToRemember: The rule 'הוא ובניו' only needs a garment with the same name for all כהנים. It does not have to be the exact same garment, so the אבנט works and the כיפה does not.

phrases.english: But according to the one who said
this is the belt of an ordinary כהן,
phrases.notes: He means the כהן גדול's יום כיפור belt matches a regular כהן's belt, so his year-round belt is a different one.

phrases.english: what is there to say?
The name 'belt' exists for everyone.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר זֶהוּ אַבְנֵטוֹ שֶׁל כֹּהֵן הֶדְיוֹט, מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty that step 13 said was still open for the second view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines what 'equal for אהרן and his sons' requires: the same name, not the same exact garment.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The garment taken for the wool size must be exactly the same for the כהן גדול and a regular כהן.
steps.terutzMaskana: Having the same name, 'belt,' is enough, so the אבנט qualifies.

steps.title: Sheared each sheep and then sold it: a disagreement
steps.stepSummary: Going back to the משנה, the גמרא brings a מחלוקת about someone who sheared a sheep and sold it, then the next one, and so on. רב חסדא says חייב, and רבי נתן בר הושעיא says פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'He did not manage to give it, etc.' It was stated: if he sheared the first sheep and sold it, רב חסדא says he is obligated and רבי נתן בר הושעיא says he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic from the משנה about ראשית הגז and presents a disagreement between two אמוראים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is someone who shears a sheep, sells it, then shears the next and sells that one too. By the end he has enough wool to owe ראשית הגז, but he no longer owns the sheep. The question is whether that still makes him obligated.

keyTerms.meaning: The first shorn wool, which must be given to a כהן
He sheared
Obligated
Exempt

phrases.english: He did not manage to give it, etc.
It was stated:
If he sheared and sold the first one,
Rav Chisda says: He is obligated,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי נָתָן בַּר הוֹשַׁעְיָא אָמַר: פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: Rabbi Natan bar Hoshaya says: He is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of the כהנים' garments and starts a new discussion on the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a מחלוקת: רב חסדא holds חייב and רבי נתן בר הושעיא holds פטור when each sheep is sold right after it is sheared.

steps.title: The reasons behind each opinion
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says he is חייב because he owned each sheep when he sheared it. רבי נתן בר הושעיא says the sheep must be 'your flock' at the moment the full amount is reached, and by then they are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא says he is obligated, since he did the shearing. רבי נתן בר הושעיא says he is exempt: at the moment the measure is completed, we need 'your flock,' and that is missing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind each side of the מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא looks at the act of shearing: each sheep was his when he sheared it, so the wool counts. רבי נתן בר הושעיא looks at the moment the obligation starts, when the five-fleece amount is complete. At that moment the sheep already belong to someone else, so they are not 'your flock.'

keyTerms.meaning: At the time
The required measure or amount
'Your flock,' from the פסוק about ראשית הגז

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the key question for the rest of the סוגיא: does ownership matter at the time of shearing, or at the time the full amount is reached?

phrases.aramaic: רַב חִסְדָּא אֲמַר חַיָּיב, דְּהָא גָּזַז.
phrases.english: Rav Chisda says he is obligated, since he sheared.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי נָתָן בַּר הוֹשַׁעְיָא אָמַר פָּטוּר,
phrases.english: Rabbi Natan bar Hoshaya says he is exempt,
because at the time the measure is completed
we need 'your flock,' and it is not there.
phrases.notes: דברים 18:4

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא אֲמַר חַיָּיב, דְּהָא גָּזַז
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning for the two opinions stated in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב חסדא: owning the sheep when shearing is enough. רבי נתן בר הושעיא: the sheep must be yours when the full amount is reached.

steps.title: Challenge from buying a גוי's sheep to shear them
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says someone who buys a גוי's fleece is פטור. That implies someone who buys the sheep themselves to shear is חייב. But for רבי נתן בר הושעיא, each sheep leaves his ownership after it is sheared, so why should he be חייב?
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: one who buys the fleece of a גוי's sheep is exempt from ראשית הגז. This implies that if he bought the sheep to shear them, he is obligated. Why? Each sheep, after its shearing, leaves his possession!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses an inference from a משנה to challenge רבי נתן בר הושעיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If buying only the wool exempts him, then buying the sheep for shearing must make him obligated. In that case each sheep goes back out of his ownership right after it is sheared, so when the five-fleece amount is reached he owns none of them. By רבי נתן בר הושעיא's reasoning he should be פטור, yet the משנה implies he is חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: One who buys
Fleece or shorn wool
This implies (introduces an inference from the משנה)
His possession or ownership

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge does not come from what the משנה says outright. It comes from what the משנה implies: buying the sheep themselves makes you obligated.

phrases.aramaic: תְּנַן: הַלּוֹקֵחַ גֵּז צֹאנוֹ שֶׁל גּוֹי,
phrases.english: We learned: One who buys the fleece of a gentile's sheep
is exempt from the first shorn wool.
This implies that if he bought his sheep to shear them, he is obligated.
Why?
Each and every one, after its shearing,
leaves his possession!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: הַלּוֹקֵחַ גֵּז צֹאנוֹ שֶׁל גּוֹי, פָּטוּר מֵרֵאשִׁית הַגֵּז. הָא צֹאנוֹ לִגְזוֹז – חַיָּיב. אַמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי נתן בר הושעיא's reasoning from step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי נתן בר הושעיא's view that the sheep must be 'your flock' when the full amount is reached.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה implies a buyer of sheep for shearing is חייב, even though each sheep leaves his ownership after shearing. That fits רב חסדא and contradicts רבי נתן בר הושעיא.

steps.title: The sheep were his for the whole thirty days
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains the משנה according to רבי נתן בר הושעיא: the גוי transferred the sheep to the buyer for the entire thirty-day period, so they were still his flock when the full amount of wool was reached.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא explained the משנה according to רבי נתן בר הושעיא: it is talking about a case where the גוי transferred the sheep to him for all thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the קשיא from Step 17 against רבי נתן בר הושעיא. It does this by describing the case in the משנה more narrowly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that each sheep seemed to leave the buyer's ownership once it was sheared. רב חסדא answers that the buyer owned all the sheep for the full thirty days. So when the total amount of wool was reached, they were still 'your flock', and he is חייב even according to רבי נתן בר הושעיא.

keyTerms.meaning: He explained it, meaning he showed how the source fits a certain view
According to the view of
He transferred ownership of them to him
Thirty days

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רבי נתן בר הושעיא's rule stays the same. The flock has to belong to the person at the moment the full amount is reached, and in this case it does.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda explained it
according to Rabbi Natan bar Hoshaya:
for example, where he (the גוי) transferred them to him
for all thirty days.
phrases.notes: Thirty days is the whole time during which he was shearing them, so he never lost ownership partway through.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּרְגְּמַאּ רַב חִסְדָּא אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי נָתָן בַּר הוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 17
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each sheep left the buyer's ownership once it was sheared, so for רבי נתן בר הושעיא it should be פטור.
steps.terutzMaskana: The buyer owned all the sheep for the full thirty days, so they were his flock when the full amount was reached.

steps.title: Who says we follow the seller if he kept some?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, about buying a friend's fleece. It asks which תנא holds that when the seller kept some wool, the obligation follows the seller.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: one who buys the fleece of his friend's flock, and so on. Who is the תנא who holds that where the seller kept some for himself, we follow the seller?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new line in the משנה. It asks which תנא is behind its rule, setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that if the seller kept some of the wool, the seller has to give ראשית הגז, not the buyer. The גמרא wants to find which earlier תנא holds this idea that 'leftover with the seller' puts the obligation on him.

keyTerms.meaning: Fleece, the wool sheared from sheep
Who is the תנא, meaning which sage's view is this
Something left over, a part the seller kept
We go after the seller, so the obligation is his

phrases.aramaic: הַלּוֹקֵחַ גֵּז צֹאנוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: One who buys the fleece of his friend's flock, etc.
Who is the תנא
who holds that where there is something left over with the seller,
we go after the seller?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line in the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that when the seller kept some, the obligation follows the seller

steps.title: It is רבי יהודה: the case of selling tree stalks
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that the משנה follows רבי יהודה. He begins quoting a משנה in פאה: someone who sells tree stalks within his field gives פאה for each one separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: it is רבי יהודה, as we learned: one who sells tree stalks within his field gives פאה for each and every one.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא names the תנא as רבי יהודה. He starts quoting a משנה from מסכת פאה to show it, beginning with the first opinion there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this משנה, the owner sells some trees in his field but not the field itself. The first opinion says the buyer gives פאה separately for each tree, because the field does not join the trees together into one unit for the buyer. This sets up רבי יהודה's comment in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Tree stalks, young trees sold to be uprooted
The corner of the field left for the poor
For each and every one separately

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the two cases apart. Here the topic is פאה on trees in a field, not wool. רב חסדא is using it as a parallel case for the idea of 'what the seller kept'.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא,
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said: It is Rabbi Yehuda,
as we learned: One who sells tree stalks
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in פאה, chapter 3.

phrases.english: within his field –
phrases.notes: He sells only the trees, not the field itself.

phrases.english: gives פאה for each and every one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא, דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of Step 19
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי יהודה, as shown from a משנה in פאה

steps.title: If the owner kept some trees, he gives פאה for all
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה limits the first ruling. The buyer gives פאה only when the field owner kept nothing. If the owner kept some trees, the owner gives פאה for all of them, which matches 'we follow the seller'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: When is this so? When the owner of the field did not keep any. But if the owner of the field kept some, he gives פאה for all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: This is רבי יהודה's comment in the משנה of פאה. It is the actual proof for רב חסדא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה says that if the seller kept some of the trees, the whole obligation of פאה falls on the seller. In the same way, the משנה about fleece says that if the seller kept some wool, the seller gives ראשית הגז. So the 'leftover with the seller' rule matches רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: When is this so? (a word that limits a ruling)
He kept some, left some for himself
The owner of the field
For everything, all of them

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's rule that 'if the seller kept some, the seller gives' follows רבי יהודה. In פאה he says that if the field owner kept some trees, the owner gives פאה for all of them.
steps.whyThisMatters: It ties the rule about ראשית הגז to one specific תנא. It also shows a shared idea: keeping a part keeps the whole obligation with the seller.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said: When is this so?
When the owner of the field did not keep any,
but if the owner of the field kept some –
he gives פאה for all of them.
phrases.notes: Here 'he' is the field owner, the seller, and not the buyer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the quote that proves Step 20
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה's rule (if the seller kept some, we follow the seller) is the view of רבי יהודה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in פאה about selling tree stalks: if the field owner kept some, he gives פאה for all

steps.title: רבא reminds רב חסדא of his own limit on רבי יהודה's ruling
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects to רב חסדא's proof. רב חסדא himself said that רבי יהודה's rule (the owner gives פאה for everything) applies only when the owner had already started harvesting.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: But aren't you the one who said that this rule applies only when the owner of the field had already begun to harvest?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges the proof from רבי יהודה that רב חסדא just brought. He quotes רב חסדא's own words back to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא had said that רבי יהודה makes the owner give פאה only if the owner started harvesting before selling. At that point the owner was already obligated. With wool, the obligation only arises later, after the sale. So the two cases do not seem to match.

keyTerms.meaning: The owner of the field (here, the seller)
To harvest or reap
But isn't it you, Master, who said: a way of challenging someone with his own earlier statement

steps.confusionAlert: The 'Master' here is רב חסדא himself, not רבי יהודה. רבא is using רב חסדא's own earlier limit against his proof.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רב חסדא, who just brought the proof from רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: But isn't it the Master who said,
This is only when the owner of the field began to harvest!
phrases.notes: He means the owner started harvesting before he sold the trees.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof from רבי יהודה given in steps 20-21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that our משנה follows רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה's ruling applies only when the seller's obligation already began before the sale. That does not fit wool, where the obligation arises after the sale.

steps.title: Why starting to shear is not like starting to harvest
steps.stepSummary: One might say the wool case also needs the seller to have started shearing. רבא rejects this. With פאה the פסוק obligates the whole field once harvesting starts, but starting to shear does not obligate the whole flock.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say that here too it is only when he began to shear: that works well there, since it is written 'And when you reap the harvest of your land,' so from the moment he starts to harvest he is obligated for the whole field. But here, from the moment he starts to shear he is not obligated for his whole flock!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא blocks a possible defense of רב חסדא. The defense says the wool case is also about a seller who started shearing before the sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In פאה, the פסוק links the obligation to the start of reaping. So once harvesting begins, the entire field is already obligated. With ראשית הגז, beginning to shear does not create an obligation on the whole flock. So the seller was never obligated for the sold sheep, and the comparison to רבי יהודה fails.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say: introduces a possible answer that is about to be rejected
It makes sense (in one case), but in the other case there is a problem
To shear (sheep)
His flock
The first shearing of wool, which is given to a כהן

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a real difference between פאה and ראשית הגז. For פאה, the whole field becomes obligated at the start of harvest. For wool, the obligation does not work that way.

phrases.english: And if you will say, so too here,
it is only when he began to shear,
granted, there,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the case of פאה in a field.

phrases.english: it is written: 'And when you reap the harvest of your land,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:9

phrases.english: from the time that he begins to harvest
he is obligated for the entire field,
but here,
from the time that he begins to shear
he is not obligated for his entire flock!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes off the obvious defense against רבא's challenge, so the challenge stands.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that our משנה is about a seller who started shearing before the sale
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Only פאה has a פסוק that obligates the whole field once harvesting begins. Starting to shear does not obligate the whole flock.

steps.title: רבא points to the משנה about buying a cow's innards
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a new answer: our משנה follows the תנא of another משנה. There, if someone buys a cow's innards that still contain the priestly gifts, the buyer gives the gifts to the כהן and cannot take their value off the price.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: It is this תנא, as we learned: If he said to him, 'Sell me the innards of this cow,' and the priestly gifts were inside them, the buyer gives them to the כהן and does not deduct their value from the money.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא drops רב חסדא's source and offers a different תנא for our משנה. He starts quoting that משנה with its first case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of comparing to פאה, רבא compares to the priestly gifts in a cow. In this first case the buyer gives the gifts to the כהן but pays the butcher full price. The assumption is that the gifts were never part of what he bought. The next line of the משנה gives the contrasting case.

keyTerms.meaning: It is this תנא: identifies which earlier sage's view the משנה follows
Innards, the inner organs of an animal
The priestly gifts from a slaughtered animal (foreleg, jaw, and maw)
Deducts their value from the price

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
It is this תנא,
phrases.notes: He means our משנה about wool follows the view of the תנא he is about to quote.

phrases.english: as we learned: If he said to him, 'Sell me'
'the innards of this cow,'
and there were priestly gifts in them,
he gives them to the כהן,
and he does not deduct them from the money.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: הַאי תַּנָּא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב חסדא's rejected answer with a new source for our משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Our משנה follows the תנא of the משנה about buying a cow's innards that contain priestly gifts.

steps.title: If he bought by weight, he may deduct the gifts
steps.stepSummary: The quoted משנה continues: if the buyer paid by weight, he still gives the gifts to the כהן, but now he may deduct their value from what he pays the butcher.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he bought from him by weight, he gives them to the כהן and deducts their value from the money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting רבא's source משנה with its contrasting second case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When buying by weight, the price included the weight of the gifts. But those gifts belonged to the כהן and were never the butcher's to sell. So the buyer gives them to the כהן and does not pay the butcher for them. This contrast with the first case is the source רבא is relying on.

keyTerms.meaning: By weight: the price is calculated by how much the item weighs
He bought from him

steps.whatToRemember: רבא rejected the comparison to רבי יהודה in פאה. Starting to harvest obligates a whole field, but starting to shear does not obligate a whole flock. He found a new source in the משנה about buying a cow's innards: buying without weighing means no deduction, while buying by weight means the buyer deducts the gifts' value.

phrases.english: If he bought from him by weight,
he gives them to the כהן
and deducts them from the money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quotation of the משנה that רבא began in step 24.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's identification of the תנא behind our משנה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about buying a cow's innards: by weight, the buyer deducts the value of the gifts; without weighing, he does not.
